assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nominal rigidities and the New Keynesian framework form the working core of modern monetary-policy analysis. Staggered price and wage setting, interest-rate rules and the microfounded policy framework are used in central banks worldwide. The result changed both academic macroeconomics and policy practice, and it has high, lasting influence.
assessment.attribution: The field is broad and the credit is shared. Calvo (staggered pricing), Taylor (staggered contracts and the policy rule) and Woodford (the synthesis and optimal-policy theory) are the most separable conceptual contributors. Gali, Christiano, Eichenbaum, Gertler and Smets made important empirical and quantitative extensions. Any three-person selection necessarily leaves out other major contributors.
assessment.maturity: The work spans roughly four decades and is thoroughly tested. It was also stress-tested through the financial crisis and the 2021-23 inflation. The Committee has not previously recognized this particular strand.
uncertainties: Whether the Committee prefers a different three-person split, or a narrower pricing-theory prize.
Criticism of the framework after the post-2008 and post-2021 episodes.
Overlap with prior macro prizes could reduce the case for it.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The heterogeneous-firm model of trade reoriented the field. It explains selection into exporting, intra-industry reallocation, and gains from trade through productivity composition. Together with the large empirical firm-level literature, it shapes how trade policy is evaluated. This is a transformative, widely applied advance.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (2003) is the clearest single anchor. Helpman's work, including Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple on exporting versus FDI, and his broader theoretical role are central. Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum (empirical firm heterogeneity) and Redding are also important and are not all in the credited set, so attribution is genuinely contested.
assessment.maturity: More than twenty years of confirmation, with extensive empirical validation and extension to quantitative general-equilibrium work. Trade has not been recognized since 2008, so the field is arguably due.
uncertainties: Whether Bernard, Jensen or Eaton should share credit.
Whether Helpman is better recognized under a different contribution, such as the trade-policy work in B013.
Magnitude of the welfare implications is debated, since gains in some models are similar to those from older frameworks.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Methods for estimating demand with differentiated products and for dynamic industry models turned empirical industrial organization into a quantitative discipline. They are standard tools in merger review, antitrust, regulation and applied work well beyond IO. Their influence is deep and practical.
assessment.attribution: The BLP random-coefficients demand framework (Berry, Levinsohn, Pakes) is the clearest triad. Pakes also contributed dynamic estimation (Ericson-Pakes, Bajari-Benkard-Levin-type work), with credit shared with Bresnahan, Reiss and Benkard. Bresnahan's and Reiss's conceptual contributions in the same area are also substantial, so attribution is not simple.
assessment.maturity: BLP dates from the mid-1990s and has been used extensively for three decades, with widely replicated applications and well-studied econometric properties.
uncertainties: Whether Bresnahan should be included.
Whether the Committee views this as methodology versus a substantive discovery.
My own field proximity (IO) may bias my sense of its importance, and I flag this as a possible conflict.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Kiyotaki-Moore (1997) showed how collateral constraints amplify and propagate shocks, giving a dynamic mechanism for credit cycles. The idea underlies much post-crisis macro-finance work and policy analysis of financial stability and amplification.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore are the clear originators of the collateral-constraint cycle model. Gertler and Gilchrist (and Bernanke, who is not in this credited set) link to the financial accelerator, so the broader theme has other contributors. The two-person attribution is clean for the collateral mechanism.
assessment.maturity: Nearly thirty years of influence, reinforced by the 2008 crisis, which brought the framework into mainstream macro modeling. Confirmation is strong, though quantitative validation varies.
uncertainties: Bernanke already has a prize, and Bernanke-Gertler-Gilchrist credit is intertwined with the theme.
Whether the Committee frames the discovery narrowly as collateral constraints or as the broader financial accelerator.
Empirical support for the mechanism is mixed across settings.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: A systematic theoretical and empirical analysis of how electoral rules, constitutions and political institutions shape fiscal policy, redistribution and state capacity. It established modern political economics as a field, with both formal models and credible cross-country and historical evidence.
assessment.attribution: Persson and Tabellini (Political Economics, constitutional-design work) are the closest pair. Besley's work on state capacity, accountability and development politics complements it. Recognition of institutions already occurred in 2024 with Acemoglu, Johnson and Robinson, so distinctness has to be argued, though the subject matter differs.
assessment.maturity: Three decades of work with extensive subsequent empirical testing. Findings on electoral rules and fiscal outcomes have been refined but remain influential.
uncertainties: Perceived overlap with the 2024 prize.
Causal identification in cross-country constitutional comparisons is debated.
Whether Besley should be included in a three-person prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Law and finance reframed how legal origins and investor protection relate to financial development and ownership. It opened a large research agenda in comparative corporate governance and had real policy influence. Vishny and Shleifer's corporate-finance and limits-to-arbitrage work adds weight.
assessment.attribution: The legal-origins and investor-protection papers are principally La Porta, Lopez-de-Silanes, Shleifer and Vishny. Shleifer's wider body of work is substantial, but the three-name limit forces a choice that excludes Vishny.
assessment.maturity: Published since the late 1990s and widely replicated and debated. Some conclusions have been qualified by later work, and the legal-origins framework itself has been challenged.
uncertainties: Robustness and interpretation of the legal-origins results.
Whether the Committee prefers Shleifer and Vishny for a broader corporate-finance and behavioral-finance contribution.
Non-scientific controversies in some laureate profiles could matter, but I treat them as outside the evidence.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Long-run series on top incomes and wealth, built from tax records, transformed the measurement of inequality and the public debate about it. Data construction at this scale is itself a scientific contribution, with direct policy relevance.
assessment.attribution: Piketty and Saez are the original top-income contributors. Zucman extended the work to wealth distribution and offshore wealth. Atkinson (deceased) was a major predecessor and collaborator, which complicates the historical credit.
assessment.maturity: The top-income series are over twenty years old and widely used. Wealth and offshore estimates are newer and more contested.
uncertainties: Methodological critiques of the wealth-concentration estimates.
Whether the Committee treats measurement and data construction as sufficient discovery.
Theoretical claims in the broader Piketty narrative are disputed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population-scale administrative data gave the first credible, granular measurements of intergenerational mobility and of how neighborhoods affect it. Chetty's wider agenda reshaped empirical public and labor economics. It is highly influential and policy-relevant.
assessment.attribution: Chetty is the clear lead across the program, with Hendren and Friedman as the most frequent collaborators. Katz's work on the Moving to Opportunity experiments is another important strand, so a three-name limit leaves out important credit.
assessment.maturity: The strongest results date from roughly 2014 onward. This is a shorter time for confirmation than the candidates ranked above, though replications in other countries are growing.
uncertainties: The work may be early for Committee consensus.
Debates over the causal interpretation of neighborhood effects and of mobility measurement.
How to apportion credit among a large collaborative group.
